chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAmr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rāshid, from ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿAnbarī, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: May a man bury his son? He said, “He should not place him in the خاک.” He said: I said, then may the son bury his father? He said, “Yes, there is no harm.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: And it should be raised above the ground by the measure of four spread fingers, no more than that. Water should be poured over it, beginning the pouring from near his head, then going around it from its four sides until he returns to the place of the head; if any water remains, he pours it onto the middle of the grave.

key_terms.أَرْبَعِ أَصَابِعَ: the measure of four fingers, describing the grave’s height
key_terms.التُّرَابِ: the earth or soil of the grave
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permitted
key_terms.مُفَرَّجَاتٍ: spread apart, qualifying the measure of the fingers
key_terms.يَدْفِنُهُ: to bury him or place him into the grave

ai.seo_question: Can a father bury his son, and how should a grave be prepared and sprinkled with water in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses rulings and etiquettes related to burial. It indicates that a father should not directly place his son into the grave, while a son may bury his father, and it also describes recommended practices for shaping the grave and pouring water over it.
